This local adapter preserves the reviewed inputs;\r\nthe host still supplies actual image handles and executes the official tool.\r\n\r\nThe names below are discovery starting points, not a frozen callable catalog.\r\n\r\n| Need | Discover and evaluate |\r\n| --- | --- |\r\n| Small standalone sprite, item or UI icon | Freeform image tools, including Pixen, Pixflux and Pro/Pro Flash; compare exact canvas, image conditioning and output count |\r\n| UI panel, frame or component set | UI asset tools; examine pieces/states, border geometry and current canvas limits |\r\n| Pixel font | Font creation and retrieval; verify required glyphs, atlas/TTF delivery and actual text rendering |\r\n| Character identity across directions | Character tools, existing-character state operations and supplied direction support |\r\n| Object/environment prop across directions | Object tools and object-state variants |\r\n| Motion | Character/object animation for an existing resource, or image animation for loose sprites; preserve timing, anchors and frame/direction expectations |\r\n| Terrain | The matching top-down, sidescroller, isometric or tile tool; reuse connected base tiles and validate adjacency |\r\n| Repair or variation | Edit/inpaint or state operations on the existing source; identify exactly what must remain unchanged |\r\n| Material response or authored effects | Normal-map and pixel/VFX workbench tools when the assignment needs those outputs |\r\n\r\nDo not choose a tool merely because “UI” or “character” appears in the task. For example, an icon's native canvas can be smaller than a UI panel operation accepts. Generate at the appropriate native scale or explain a proposed adaptation; resizing an oversized result is not automatically equivalent pixel art.\r\n\r\nInspect output cardinality before submission: a candidate grid, eight directions and one image are different deliverables. Do not order additional variants just because a mode returns them. Query capability/quote tools where available; preserve their provisional meaning and the user's current limits. No cached price or old tool inventory establishes the current charge or entitlement.\r\n\r\n## Preserve reference meaning in actual arguments\r\n\r\nAssign each visual input a role before selecting the operation:\r\n\r\n| Role | Preserve |\r\n| --- | --- |\r\n| style | Art language: selected palette/ramp behavior, outlines, shading, detail and cluster scale |\r\n| identity | The particular subject, costume, silhouette or already approved sprite |\r\n| pose | Orientation, gesture, contact and anatomical placement |\r\n| layout | Spatial arrangement, UI pieces, safe areas or composition |\r\n| palette | Explicit color choices when adopted, rather than incidental reference measurements |\r\n| mask | The actual region to change/preserve with the selected tool's mask semantics |\r\n| motion | Timing/pose sequence or motion reference |\r\n\r\nPLAR's optional `references` entries record `source`, `role` and `instructions`. Sources bind actual project files; selected context carries their current identities. A source citation or a filename written in a text prompt does **not** transmit an image to PixelLab.\r\n\r\nInspect the chosen tool's image inputs. For an image on disk, discover `get_upload_url` first when the operation accepts an image URL. Follow its returned upload instructions to send the file bytes directly (for example, multipart `curl -F file=@PATH`; `curl.exe` on Windows), parse the actual response, and use its returned `upload:<id>` in the corresponding image URL field. Bind that handle to the original local hash and role in the reviewed request. Keep the temporary upload URL out of delivery artifacts. This avoids model transcription of encoded image data; manually pasted base64 can corrupt even a small PNG.\r\n\r\nTransfer the actual image via its supported upload URL/handle, owned source ID, URL or encoded payload. Use `get_upload_url` and its returned instructions for local images when available; prefer supported handles/URLs to large inline base64. Keep the local source hash, its role, the returned handle and the exact request field associated in production evidence. Upload handles are temporary transport references, not durable replacements for local source files.\r\n\r\nUse the role-specific input: a style anchor is not necessarily a subject/pose source, and an init image can influence composition as well as appearance. Reusing an approved character or object ID can preserve identity more directly than describing it again. For Pro Flash, inspect current native sizes and style-image fit; the style anchor and content-reference count are distinct concepts. Reuse the chosen family anchor and relevant controls across members, then inspect the actual results.\r\n\r\nIf the chosen operation cannot express a required reference role, select a supported operation or propose a concrete staged workflow. A text-only fallback needs to be identified as an approximation; do not present it as equivalent reference conditioning. Avoid adding an unrelated exact-palette restriction merely because a style image has a small measured color set.\r\n\r\nThe [style-reference workflow](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs/tools/consistent-style) explains style consistency, while [init-image options](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs/options/init-image) explain image-guided generation. Their editor controls do not substitute for the live MCP input schema. The [UI workflow](https://www.pixellab.ai/docs/tools/create-ui-elements-pro) informs design intent; verify the actual MCP UI operation's limits independently.\r\n\r\n## Run and review\r\n\r\nUse [provider recovery](provider-recovery.md) for saved intent and actual calls. Capture returned IDs, use the matching retrieval tool, and use bounded `wait_for_jobs` when appropriate instead of blind repeated polling. Retrieve actual output files before inspection.\r\n\r\nReview the asset's intended function at its display size: state readability for UI, identity and volume across directions, timing and contact in playback, adjacency in terrain, and alpha/material behavior in the target renderer. Keep source art and failed candidates. Prefer a targeted edit of a nearly correct result when it preserves the required identity; do not erase the original.\r\n\r\nFor animation, distinguish requested generated frames from the tool's returned\r\nsequence: some operations include the supplied input frame in addition to generated\r\nframes. Retain every returned frame, declare any selection/assembly explicitly,\r\nand check the consumer's exact frame count and last-to-first transition. A provider\r\nclaim of transparency is not a per-frame alpha check. Inspect each actual frame for\r\nmatte leaks, shape drift and unintended holds before acceptance.\r\n\r\nUse the host's pixel-art judgment and the official platform's deterministic editing\r\ntools when they better preserve a useful generated result. Retain the source,\r\nguard edits against observed pixels and verify what changed. Distinguish a generated\r\npose with specialist-constructed motion from motion produced by an animation model;\r\nboth can serve the asset, but their provenance and quality evidence differ. A failed\r\nbackground-removal attempt can leave a useful opaque retry requiring an explicitly\r\nreviewed cutout. Preserve the failed attempt and review the corrected candidate anew.\r\n\r\nReturn the [caller result](delegation.md) with files, checks, remaining questions and real provider/state identifiers. The platform creates candidates; the specialist supplies design judgment and evidence of fit.\r\n# Provider submission and recovery operation\r\n\r\nUse this operation when a PIXL production task needs an external generation request, a submitted attempt needs resumption, or a returned candidate needs to enter project state. Developing this operation is a maintainer task; only a production assignment or explicit evaluation activates PIXL.\r\n\r\nRead the [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md), its [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json), and the [journal contract](../../../resources/spec/provider-recovery.md). This operation uses the explicit J.jr/op/xs extension. Existing unjournaled J and PX1 stores keep their earlier meanings; adding fields or changing a header does not manufacture durable history.\r\n\r\n## Required context\r\n\r\n- The project root, current store state/hash, task and selected planned F outputs. Use the [intake/sample operation](intake-sample.md) first if choices or criteria are missing. Sample tasks may test proposals; dependent production still needs adoption and confirmation.\r\n- The actual connected provider identity, selected tool and exact inputSchema observed through this harness, with a retained discovery source, timestamp and evidence. A cached capabilities list is advisory. If live tools are absent, preserve the plan and explain the missing capability; do not invent a discovery observation.\r\n- The user's established authorized scope and budget, retained as a scope string and evidence object. Existing authorization can support this record; a local tool does not grant new authority. Resolve a consequential missing budget/permission before a paid call while continuing independent work.\r\n- For recovery, the saved intent and every retained observation. For import, the actual already downloaded file and evidence relating it to this returned resource. Keep credentials out of arguments, schema examples, discovery, authorization and response evidence.\r\n\r\nResolve `../../../scripts/pixl.py` relative to this reference directory and invoke its absolute path using the selected Python environment. The commands below omit that common prefix. Use the same project `--root ROOT` throughout; STORE is a subdirectory of ROOT. Every mutation consumes the current `--expect HASH` and returns the next hash. Files and evidence belong in the project, outside installed resources.\r\n\r\n## Prepare a saved request\r\n\r\nPrefer the actual connected official PixelLab MCP operation when it fits the task. Use [operation and reference selection](pixellab-operations.md) first: confirm the native canvas, reference roles and output packaging. Preserve image transport identifiers with their local source hashes. The optional HTTP route below is a selected integration, not a substitute for every MCP workflow.\r\n\r\nWhen the host exposes the optional PixelLab HTTP bridge, use `pixellab_contract`\r\nto inspect its retained official HTTP schema, source date and simulated/live flag.\r\nIt currently supports one async image operation. This is a dated HTTP contract,\r\nnot live MCP discovery; HTTP `image_size` is distinct from MCP width/height aliases.\r\n`pixellab_prepare_image` validates and saves the request against the planned task\r\nand output. Then `pixellab_submit` claims, submits once and records the response;\r\ndo not call local `job-dispatch` first. `pixellab_poll` observes the saved ID once\r\n(allow the returned interval between real polls), and `pixellab_import_image`\r\ndecodes and retains a completed response as an unaccepted candidate. Each mutation\r\nrequires the current store hash. Continue with normal inspection and acceptance.\r\nUnknown submission outcomes cannot be resubmitted; preserve and reconcile them.\r\nMocked bridge observations remain simulated, including in handoffs.\r\n\r\n1. Run `workflow STORE/state.px --root ROOT` and `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. Read both lifecycle blockers and existing provider attempts. An open task does not imply permission to create another remote job. Pending prepared/unknown/submitted/running work on the output must be resolved first.\r\n2. Retrieve the task's focused context. Translate its intended output and relevant inputs, decisions, methods and contract into the actual tool schema. Preserve arguments exactly; describe any requirement the tool cannot express and the later acceptance check that will evaluate it.\r\n3. Write a request JSON object with exactly `provider`, `tool`, `arguments`, `schema`, `discovery`, and `authorization`. `schema` is the full inputSchema object. Discovery has `source`, `observed_at`, `evidence`; authorization has `scope`, `evidence`. Evidence must be nonempty objects. Timestamps require an explicit UTC offset and at most six fractional digits. Capture observation time from the host clock when observing/recording the response (for example, Python datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()); keep provider event time separate. Do not invent a precise time from the session date, and omit optional timestamps that were not observed. Values come from the current assignment and observations, not from a bundled art fixture.\r\n4. Run `job-prepare STORE JOB TASK REQUEST_JSON --outputs OUTPUT ... --expect HASH --root ROOT`. This saves exact request/schema/provenance/authorization and the relevant plan hashes. Read its cached assessment: a conflict is a reason to inspect current documentation and tool semantics, not to silently rewrite the request or substitute the cache for the observed schema. Schema validity alone cannot establish account entitlement, output quality or actual cost.\r\n\r\nPreparation is complete when state contains the prepared J and immutable journal X/E. No remote action has occurred. A missing tool, unresolved project requirement or missing authorization leaves useful local planning intact.\r\n\r\n## Claim once, then call the actual provider\r\n\r\nRun `job-dispatch STORE JOB --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Only a successful publication returns `dispatch_request`. It first records a local dispatch claim and moves the saved job to **unknown**, before the host sends anything. Use exactly the returned provider/tool/arguments for the one authorized host call. Do not add defaults or replace arguments after claiming; that would be a different request.\r\n\r\nThe local command does not submit, poll, authenticate or download. `remote_executed: false` describes the local tool even when its journal later records a caller-observed success. Real provider effects remain the host's responsibility.\r\n\r\nRetain the response without credentials and use `job-observe STORE JOB STATE EVIDENCE_JSON --remote-id RETURNED_ID --expect HASH --root ROOT`. Accepted states submitted/running/succeeded require the actual observed identifier. A supplied failure can be recorded without inventing an ID. After identity is known, omitting `--remote-id` preserves it; it cannot be rebound. Repeat running/unknown observations only when supported by actual observations. A failed or succeeded outcome is terminal for observations.\r\n\r\nIf submission returns no usable answer, record `unknown` with the actual timeout/transport evidence when available. Never treat the initial unknown claim as evidence that a provider received the request, and never treat a missing ID as evidence that it did not.\r\n\r\nFor delegated work, compare the saved prepared request with the exact arguments in the [reviewed request packet](request-review.md) before dispatch. Changed arguments or criteria require an updated comparison; an unchanged reviewed contract does not require the user to repeat authorization.\r\n\r\n## Resume and reconcile\r\n\r\nStart with `jobs STORE/state.px --root ROOT`. It returns the saved request, context, event history, remote identity, candidate associations, drift and next action. Reading a request is not a new dispatch grant.\r\n\r\nA resource ID belongs to the connection that returned it. Use that same provider/account context for lookup or retrieval; never carry a simulated or unrelated provider ID into a real service. If the originating connection cannot return an image, retain that limitation and its observed state. Separate future production uses its own actual request and provider identity under the assignment; it is not retrieval of the simulated job. A finished request-only assignment does not terminate its queued job: before another request for the same asset, resolve the pending attempt with supported originating-connection evidence, or keep a truly separate assignment/context explicit. Changing task/output IDs within the asset store cannot bypass its pending attempt.\r\n\r\n| Saved state / issue | Next operation |\r\n|---|---|\r\n| Prepared, context current, no blockers | Claim with job-dispatch before one host call |\r\n| Prepared, plan drift or lifecycle blocker | Resolve the specific context; abandon obsolete intent with an evidenced failed observation if appropriate, then prepare a new request ID |\r\n| Unknown | Reconcile using the actual provider's documented lookup/status capabilities and retained evidence; do not dispatch or recreate |\r\n| Submitted/running with ID | Inspect that exact resource using its discovered status tool, then record the observed response |\r\n| Succeeded | Retrieve the actual output through the host, import local candidate bytes, then evaluate acceptance |\r\n| Failed | Preserve failure, establish its consequence and any still-valid retry authorization, then use a new job ID for a new attempt |\r\n| Legacy unjournaled job | Inspect its actual available history manually; do not attach a fictional journal or ignore pending work |\r\n| File/hash error | Preserve the diagnostic and restore the exact retained bytes from available history/backups before continuing; do not rewrite receipts to make a changed file pass |\r\n\r\nA crash between claim and host submission also leaves unknown. If no provider lookup can resolve whether the request was sent, leave that uncertainty explicit and continue independent work. Elapsed time cannot authorize a retry. A confirmed non-acceptance or terminal failure may support a failed observation and a newly authorized attempt; record that evidence first. Automatic remote exactly-once delivery is not claimed.\r\n\r\nOn `stale_write` or `store_locked`, no dispatch grant was returned. Reread the state and owner information, then reconcile the attempted local change. Do not blindly repeat job-dispatch if another writer already claimed it. Immutable blobs left by a failed publication are unreferenced preparation data; state.px is the publication authority.\r\n\r\n## Import and hand back to acceptance\r\n\r\nDownload with the actual host/provider mechanism into the project. Then run `job-import STORE JOB OUTPUT CANDIDATE DOWNLOADED_PATH EVIDENCE_JSON --expect HASH --root ROOT`. DOWNLOADED_PATH is relative to ROOT. This copies a byte snapshot into the store and creates X.of for the original F, plus a retained import event and J.xs reference. It preserves the downloaded original. It does not nominate the candidate, measure the image, grant V, or finish T.\r\n\r\nImport rejects changed output/contract/criterion context. Keep the returned file and original history; reconcile the intended plan explicitly before associating it. A new interpretation must not relabel an old generation as though it used the new contract. Submitted observations can still be recorded while the plan has drifted.\r\n\r\nRetrieve the imported X to obtain its retained path/hash. Run relevant mechanical inspection, review the actual image at native and enlarged scale, and exercise the required destination checks. Follow the [intake/sample acceptance procedure](intake-sample.md) to nominate a candidate deliberately and record each Q's pass, fail or unavailable verdict. Provider success and journal-retention receipts cannot satisfy those requirements.\r\n\r\nThe operation stops with a truthful recovery action or an imported candidate ready for its specified acceptance checks. Handoff includes the job and candidate IDs, actual observed state, retained paths, unresolved checks and the next dependency. No finished asset family or engine readiness follows from this local operation alone.\r\n"}

        "text": "# Revising a drawing — `changes` and `inspect`\n\nAfter `draw` renders, revise with small, reasoned changes instead of\nrewriting the recipe. Each call appends to the drawing's change list, rebuilds\neverything from the original sources, and shows a before/after with change\nmasks against the drawing you revised.\n\n```\npixelart_workbench(argv=[\"draw\", \"--drawing\", \"<id>\", \"--changes\", \"[ …operations… ]\"])\npixelart_workbench(argv=[\"draw\", \"--drawing\", \"<id>\", \"--inspect\", \"[ …crops… ]\"])\n```\n\nEvery operation needs `operation`, `frames` (one-based) and `reason`.\n\n**Pose / drawing** — `set_node` overrides a node on chosen frames (`at`, `pivot`,\n`angle`, `opacity`, `visible`, or a replacement `draw` list):\n\n```json\n{\"operation\": \"set_node\", \"view\": \"south\", \"node\": \"arm\", \"frames\": [3],\n \"values\": {\"angle\": -140, \"at\": {\"node\": \"root\", \"point\": [1, 0]}},\n \"reason\": \"The raised arm clips the head; move it out and lower it a little.\"}\n```\n\n**Structure** — these two edit the drawing itself rather than chosen frames,\nso they take `view` and `reason`, not `frames` (only `add_node` has an optional\n`frames`: the frames it shows on):\n- `add_node` — `{\"operation\": \"add_node\", \"view\": \"south\", \"node\": \"spark\",\n  \"values\": {\"layer\": \"fx\", \"at\": [30, 12], \"draw\": [ … ]}, \"frames\": [3, 4],\n  \"reason\": \"…\"}`. With `frames` it shows on those frames only; `after` names the\n  node it draws after. No placeholder nodes needed.\n- `set_track` — `{\"operation\": \"set_track\", \"view\": \"south\", \"node\": \"arm\",\n  \"property\": \"angle\", \"keys\": [[1, 0], [3, -140]], \"reason\": \"…\"}` replaces\n  that node's track for that property (optional `interpolation`/`anchor`, as in\n  the recipe). Works on a view timed by `tracks`, or on a still view, which it\n  gives its first track; a view timed by `poses`/`frames` changes with `set_node`.\n  Tracks run first; a `set_node` on the same frames overrides them.\n\nTo remove a node, send the recipe again without it — a fresh `draw` costs the\nsame as a revision.\n\n**Timing** — `{\"operation\": \"duration\", \"frames\": [3], \"milliseconds\": 200,\n\"reason\": \"Hold the peak longer.\"}` (10 ms steps; applies to every view).\n\n**Pixels on a layer** — every `edit` operation works here too, with\n`view` and a layer **name** as printed in the response (`\"Body - right arm\"`):\n\n```json\n{\"operation\": \"patch_pixels\", \"view\": \"south\", \"layer\": \"Body - right arm\",\n \"frames\": [2, 3], \"pixels\": [[43, 22, \"#f0c8a0ff\", \"#221c1aff\"]],\n \"reason\": \"Close the outline gap at the elbow.\"}\n```\n\nGuards check the colour ON THAT LAYER, which can differ from the flattened\nimage — read it first with a layer inspection. Raster fixes run after posing, so\na later `set_node` can move pixels out from under an old patch: re-inspect.\nMirrored views follow their original automatically; edit the original.\n\n**Inspect** — enlarged crops of the current render:\n\n```json\n[{\"view\": \"south\", \"mode\": \"body\", \"frames\": [2, 3, 4], \"region\": [30, 10, 50, 40], \"scale\": 10},\n {\"view\": \"south\", \"mode\": \"layer\", \"layer\": \"Body - right arm\", \"frames\": [3], \"region\": [36, 12, 48, 30]}]\n```\n\n`full` = everything, `body` = body layers only, `layer` = one layer, and also\nreturns that layer's exact colours per pixel (palette-indexed) for guards.\n\nThe engine contract below was written for its command line: its decision\nenvelope (`candidate_id` / `decision: \"edit\"|\"inspect\"|\"finish\"`) is what these\ntwo parameters replace — send only the operations. `finish` is not needed; the\nuser judges the result. Here: `edit <id> --changes` is its PNG/GIF worker — send only the `changes` list (no `version` / `source_sha256` envelope; `layer` defaults to \"image\"). `draw` is its animation job — a `recipe` is a job + scene, `--changes` and `--inspect` replace its edit/inspect decisions, and finish is not needed. Ignore file paths, commands and experiment links; the server fills every path field.\n\n---\n\n# Python animation jobs\n\nRender and revise layered pixel animation with Python, NumPy and Pillow. No Aseprite, display, GPU, model service or API key is required. Mount prepared input jobs under `/app/jobs`, then run `pixel-animation build /app/jobs/job.json --out /app/jobs/run-001`. The Docker definition has not been built or deployed here.\n\n## What stays reusable\n\n| Component | Responsibility |\n| --- | --- |\n| `server/pixel_renderer.py` | Pixel rasterization, layers, polygon transforms, two-bone IK and common shapes |\n| `server/pixel_ops.py` | Normal RGBA compositing and inverse-sampled bitmap transforms |\n| `server/pixel_edits.py` | Guarded pixel patches, simultaneous color tables, reference-region copying and exact palette inspection |\n| `server/drawing_renderer.py` | General JSON drawing, source cutouts, named poses and anchors |\n| `server/articulated_renderer.py` | Current action template, source-part posing, VFX and direction mirroring |\n| Scene JSON and label PNGs | Character-specific pivots, limbs, source-part assignment, pose keys, colors and layer order |\n| `tools/animation_job.py` | Validation, rendering, exports, provenance, comparisons and review decisions |\n| Model or human reviewer | Motion intent, preservation judgments, observations and bounded edits |\n\nLayer archives are numeric `.npz` files with arrays shaped `[frame, y, x, RGBA]`, loaded with `numpy.load(path, allow_pickle=False)`. `frames.json` maps archive keys to named body/VFX layers and includes durations, tags and drawing-node anchors. Set it to `false` in a trusted job only when the requested restyle intentionally changes the first/rest pose; raw first/last equality remains in `reference_comparisons` in the result and review packet. This does not disable protected-region, palette, timing or export checks. The existing `body_palette_exact` setting controls whether new body colors are permitted.\n\n## Visual feedback loop\n\n1. Inspect the original artwork, the intended action and all supplied directions. Preserve identity, native pixels and source palette. Record protected features and intended effects before editing.\n2. Build a candidate. Open `packet.json` and **attach its PNG evidence** to the model, or open the files directly in Codex. Generating a packet does not send images or constitute review.\n3. Review numbered full/body sheets covering every frame, 10x nearest-neighbor source views, and palette swatches. The packet includes source, effect and actual output palettes. Sheets default to 2x to fit useful frame groups. Request 8–10x matching crops for ambiguous details instead of enlarging an entire animation indiscriminately.\n4. Return `inspect`, `edit` or `finish`. Batch related edits. An edit rebuilds from pinned inputs into a new run, propagates original-view edits to mirrors, and creates changed-pixel counts, numbered masks, before/after key-frame PNGs and comparison GIFs against its immediate parent.\n5. A model receiving a GIF file must not assume it has watched every frame.\n6. Once the motion works, review pixel polish separately. Inspect joints, overlapping parts, cloth/equipment boundaries, outlines and small detached clusters in matching 8–10x crops with adjacent poses. Moved source cutouts can carry neighboring material pixels even when palette and renderer-parity checks pass. Use exact layer inspection and batch guarded `patch_pixels` for observed local defects; save the patches after posing so rebuilds retain them. Open the new comparison and change masks, then check all final frames and the loop again. Do not force edits when no defect is observed or send one model call per pixel.\n7. Supported change objects:\n\n```json\n[\n  {\"operation\":\"duration\",\"frames\":[22],\"milliseconds\":80,\"reason\":\"Release needs a longer hold.\"},\n  {\"operation\":\"pose_key\",\"frames\":[22],\"values\":{\"torso_lean_deg\":-10,\"arm_spread\":0.9},\"reason\":\"The release pose is too extended.\"},\n  {\"operation\":\"pixels\",\"view\":\"east\",\"layer\":\"VFX - sparks\",\"frames\":[23],\"pixels\":[[180,90,\"#00000000\"]],\"reason\":\"Remove an observed stray spark.\"},\n  {\"operation\":\"replace_color\",\"view\":\"east\",\"layer\":\"VFX - core light\",\"frames\":[22],\"region\":[120,70,159,109],\"from\":\"#ffffff\",\"to\":\"#ffe5b5\",\"reason\":\"Use the intended warm highlight.\"}\n]\n```\n\nThese are syntax examples, not instructions to apply those edits to the sample. `pixels` and `replace_color` address original views only; mirrors follow automatically. `duration` applies to every direction, in 10 ms steps. `pose_key` edits an existing shared keyframe using any of `forward_root`, `crouch`, `torso_lean_deg`, `arm_fold`, `arm_spread`, `foot_stride`, `foot_lift`, `head_counter_rotation_deg`. # Python animation jobs

Render and revise layered pixel animation with Python, NumPy and Pillow. No Aseprite, display, GPU, model service or API key is required. The worker renders JSON-controlled animation; a separate caller supplies visual judgments.

For new actions, use `python-drawing` with a `layered-drawing-v1` scene. It supports arbitrary frame counts, named source parts, drawing primitives, reusable poses, anchored equipment and JSON node edits. Read the [drawing scene format](DRAWING_SCENES.md) and use the [eight-frame archer test](../experiments/python-drawing-v2/README.md) as a compact example. New artwork and motion still need to be designed and reviewed; the worker does not turn a text prompt into animation by itself.

The older `python-articulated` backend and `articulated-burst-v1` template remain a regression fixture for Umbra Core. That template has a fixed 44-frame phase schedule and should not be selected automatically for unrelated actions.

For walk cycles and other repeated motion, the [cyclic motion workflow](MOTION_WORKFLOW.md) adds source-part selection, compact pose tracks, onion-skin evidence and foot-anchor checks. It compiles into the same drawing backend. Identical full/body review sheets are deduplicated and declared in `equivalent_evidence_modes`; both underlying exports remain available.

## Run a job

From the workspace root, with `server/requirements.txt` installed:

```sh
python tools/animation_job.py build experiments/python-drawing-v2/final-job.json --out experiments/my-animation/run-001
python tools/animation_job.py decide experiments/my-animation/run-001 decision.json --out experiments/my-animation/run-002
```

The first command renders; the second accepts `inspect` or `edit` decisions. `finish` records a review in the existing run and does not take `--out`. Output directories must be new and inside the workspace. Existing runs and input pixels remain intact. Job asset paths resolve from the workspace root; part-map paths resolve from the scene directory. Supply trusted job configuration and asset paths from your application, not arbitrary public request bodies.

For a queue worker, import `prepare_job`, `build`, and `decide` from `tools.animation_job`. `build(prepare_job(job_path), output_path)` returns the result dictionary. `decide(run_path, decision_dict, output_path)` applies validated structured feedback. The CLI and Python functions share the same implementation. A web endpoint, queue and storage adapter are outside this prototype.

The [small sample](../experiments/python-drawing-v2/README.md) documents the drawing comparison; the [older reproduction](../experiments/streamlined-animation-v1/README.md) remains available. For a Linux worker image, build from the repository root with `docker build -f server/animation.Dockerfile -t pixel-animation .`. Mount prepared input jobs under `/app/jobs`, then run `pixel-animation build /app/jobs/job.json --out /app/jobs/run-001`. The Docker definition has not been built or deployed here.

## What stays reusable

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `server/pixel_renderer.py` | Pixel rasterization, layers, polygon transforms, two-bone IK and common shapes |
| `server/pixel_ops.py` | Normal RGBA compositing and inverse-sampled bitmap transforms |
| `server/pixel_edits.py` | Guarded pixel patches, simultaneous color tables, reference-region copying and exact palette inspection |
| `server/drawing_renderer.py` | General JSON drawing, source cutouts, named poses and anchors |
| `server/articulated_renderer.py` | Current action template, source-part posing, VFX and direction mirroring |
| Scene JSON and label PNGs | Character-specific pivots, limbs, source-part assignment, pose keys, colors and layer order |
| `tools/animation_job.py` | Validation, rendering, exports, provenance, comparisons and review decisions |
| Model or human reviewer | Motion intent, preservation judgments, observations and bounded edits |

Layer archives are numeric `.npz` files with arrays shaped `[frame, y, x, RGBA]`, loaded with `numpy.load(path, allow_pickle=False)`. `frames.json` maps archive keys to named body/VFX layers and includes durations, tags and drawing-node anchors. Exports include full and body-only PNG sheets, GIFs and a shared HTML viewer with one clock, integer zoom and consistent backgrounds.

The drawing backend supports normal alpha compositing and node opacity. PNG sheets and layer archives retain partial alpha. GIF cannot: declare an opaque `gif_background` such as `#52596e` to produce an explicitly matted GIF preview when needed. Otherwise partial-alpha GIF export is rejected. A GIF exceeding the exact encoder's palette capacity is skipped (reported as `gif_omitted`) instead of being silently quantized; the PNG sheets and layers stay exact. The legacy burst backend still uses binary alpha.

For requested outline styling, use the [outline operations](OUTLINE_TOOLS.md). Jobs default to `source_bookends_exact: true`. Set it to `false` in a trusted job only when the requested restyle intentionally changes the first/rest pose; raw first/last equality remains in `reference_comparisons` in the result and review packet. This does not disable protected-region, palette, timing or export checks. The existing `body_palette_exact` setting controls whether new body colors are permitted.

## Visual feedback loop

1. Inspect the original artwork, the intended action and all supplied directions. Preserve identity, native pixels and source palette. Record protected features and intended effects before editing.
2. Build a candidate. Open `packet.json` and **attach its PNG evidence** to the model, or open the files directly in Codex. Generating a packet does not send images or constitute review.
3. Review numbered full/body sheets covering every frame, 10x nearest-neighbor source views, and palette swatches. The packet includes source, effect and actual output palettes. Sheets default to 2x to fit useful frame groups. Request 8–10x matching crops for ambiguous details instead of enlarging an entire animation indiscriminately.
4. Return `inspect`, `edit` or `finish`. Batch related edits. An edit rebuilds from pinned inputs into a new run, propagates original-view edits to mirrors, and creates changed-pixel counts, numbered masks, before/after key-frame PNGs and comparison GIFs against its immediate parent.
5. Inspect the new evidence and affected neighbors. Check body motion separately from effects. Check playback, light/dark backgrounds and the loop seam in `index.html`. A model receiving a GIF file must not assume it has watched every frame.
6. Once the motion works, review pixel polish separately. Inspect joints, overlapping parts, cloth/equipment boundaries, outlines and small detached clusters in matching 8–10x crops with adjacent poses. Moved source cutouts can carry neighboring material pixels even when palette and renderer-parity checks pass. Use exact layer inspection and batch guarded `patch_pixels` for observed local defects; save the patches after posing so rebuilds retain them. Open the new comparison and change masks, then check all final frames and the loop again. Do not force edits when no defect is observed or send one model call per pixel.
7. Accept only after technical checks and visual review pass. If playback or another required check is unavailable, record a `partial` result with the remaining issue. Stop after two edit/review passes without observed improvement and return the best reviewed candidate with limitations; this is a caller policy, not an automatic worker loop.

The worker does not invoke a model. This keeps subscription testing and a future API reviewer interchangeable. It also means CPU renders use zero model tokens; development and visual review still consume tokens. Pixel equality to a reference proves reproduction, not that an unfamiliar animation meets the user's intent.

Use the [compact review prompt](animation-review.prompt.md) with the user's intent, the operation contract and the current packet. Subsequent turns need the latest decision and new evidence rather than the renderer source or the full development conversation.

## Decision contract

All decisions contain the exact `candidate_id` from `result.json`. Frames are **one-based**. Pixel coordinates are **zero-based**, relative to the padded canvas; rectangles include both endpoints. Unknown fields, operations, layer names and invalid bounds are rejected. Colors are `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`, with alpha `00` or `ff`.

Legacy `pixels` and `replace_color` edits retain the binary-alpha restriction. Drawing-node commands can contain partial alpha. The [pixel editing contract](PIXEL_EDIT_TOOLS.md) adds `patch_pixels`, `map_colors`, `copy_region`, and exact layer/palette inspection to `python-drawing`, plus a direct PNG/GIF entry point. These share one implementation and report per-operation pixel changes. For pose and drawing changes, use `set_node`:

```json
{"operation":"set_node","view":"south","node":"bow","frames":[2,7],"values":{"at":[55,48]},"reason":"Move the rising bow clear of the hair; its anchored hand follows."}
```

Node edits can change `at`, `pivot`, `angle`, `opacity`, `visible`, or `draw`. A replacement `draw` list can redraw a shape, restore a source region, or change outlines without writing Python. Anchor cycles and unsupported commands are rejected. The scene format describes the actual supported commands. `pose_key` below applies only to the older articulated backend.

Inspection:

```json
{
  "candidate_id": "COPY_FROM_RESULT",
  "decision": "inspect",
  "inspections": [{
    "view": "east", "mode": "body", "frames": [21, 22, 23],
    "region": [120, 70, 159, 109], "scale": 10,
    "reason": "Check the hand and torso through release."
  }]
}
```

An edit has `candidate_id`, `decision: "edit"` and a nonempty `changes` array. Supported change objects:

```json
[
  {"operation":"duration","frames":[22],"milliseconds":80,"reason":"Release needs a longer hold."},
  {"operation":"pose_key","frames":[22],"values":{"torso_lean_deg":-10,"arm_spread":0.9},"reason":"The release pose is too extended."},
  {"operation":"pixels","view":"east","layer":"VFX - sparks","frames":[23],"pixels":[[180,90,"#00000000"]],"reason":"Remove an observed stray spark."},
  {"operation":"replace_color","view":"east","layer":"VFX - core light","frames":[22],"region":[120,70,159,109],"from":"#ffffff","to":"#ffe5b5","reason":"Use the intended warm highlight."}
]
```

These are syntax examples, not instructions to apply those edits to the sample. `pixels` and `replace_color` address original views only; mirrors follow automatically. `duration` applies to every direction, in 10 ms steps. `pose_key` edits an existing shared keyframe using any of `forward_root`, `crouch`, `torso_lean_deg`, `arm_fold`, `arm_spread`, `foot_stride`, `foot_lift`, `head_counter_rotation_deg`. Root-motion metadata follows the edited curve. This template's native rest frames and fixed effect phases still apply.

A finish decision contains exactly:

- `candidate_id`, `decision: "finish"`, `status: "accepted"` or `"partial"`.
- `reviewed_evidence`: map of actually viewed relative PNG paths to their supplied SHA-256 hashes.
- `visual_checks`: boolean judgments for `source_fidelity`, `articulation`, `equipment_contact`, `effects`, `clipping`, `loop_transition`.
- `playback_verified`: boolean, and `unresolved`: list of remaining issues.

Acceptance requires all listed evidence, all visual checks true, verified playback, passing technical checks and no unresolved issues. File hashes reject stale decisions and changed deliverables. The review is explicitly **caller-attested**: JSON cannot prove that a human or model actually examined the images.

## Validation

Run `python -m unittest server.test_drawing_renderer tools.test_animation_job tools.test_drawing_pipeline -v`. Protected regions in a view can enforce exact pixels or preserve the original visible source pixels throughout the body timeline. Use them for features intended to stay still; palette equality alone does not detect erased details.

{"name":"mcp__pixellab__pixelart_workbench","description":"Run one pixel-art command on a drawing or image you already made. This is
the engine's own command line: it checks work, explains it and improves it.

Commands: check and explain (read-only):
- lint <id> [--rules outline_gap,orphan_pixel,…] — pixel-art defects, each
  naming the node and command that drew them
- inspect <id> --region x0,y0,x1,y1 --scale 10 — a zoomed crop with its
  exact colours
- measure <id> --at x,y — what is at a pixel and who drew it
- explain <id> — resolved geometry, per-command footprints, before rendering
- motion / storyboard / silhouette / reveal / clusters / parts <id> — reports
- score <id> — a 0-100 pixel-art discipline score with a breakdown
- compare <id> <id> — two results side by side
Improve (returns a NEW drawing id):
- shade <id> --band 2 --light=-1,-1 — banded shading along a colour ramp
- selout <id> — selective outlining; reoutline / clean-lines / aa / mirror
- cluster <id> --at x,y --action recolor --color <name> — one guarded cluster
- repair <id> — deterministic cleanup of drift, strays, fringe and noise
Sheets and frames (returns a NEW image id):
- split <image> --grid 3x3 — a sprite sheet, strip or grid as an animation,
  one frame per cell (columns x rows)
- join <image> <image> … [--as sheet|rows|animation] [--columns n] — pictures
  or animations as one sprite sheet, one per row, or one animation
- scale <image> --by 4 — the same picture or animation bigger, each pixel a
  4x4 block (a sticker, a print); nothing is redrawn
A result comes back as an image in the reply AND as a no-auth URL the reply
prints, `/mcp/pixel-tools/<id>/image.png` (`frames.png` for the frames of a
multi-frame one) — so a sheet you joined is both readable inline and
downloadable. Sheets hold at most 1024 px a side; `join` refuses a larger
one rather than shrinking the art, and says how many frames do fit.
Craft operations need colour ramps: run `extract-palette <id>` first, then
pass `--ramps skin=dark,mid,light`.
Authoring: `edit <id> --changes '[…]'` applies exact pixel operations and
`draw <id> --recipe '{…}'` builds or revises a layered scene; both take JSON
whose fields are NOT listed here. Colours in that JSON are always `#RRGGBB`
or `#RRGGBBAA` with alpha `00` or `ff` — `rgb()` and bare hex are refused,
and nothing strips the `#`, since argv is a JSON list rather than a shell
line. Every `edit` change carries `operation`, `layer`, `frames` (ONE-based)
and `reason`; coordinates are zero-based and a `region` is `[x0,y0,x1,y1]`
inclusive. Then its own fields: `patch_pixels` takes `pixels`, a list of
`[x,y,expected,replacement]` (1-10000, each assigned only where the pixel
already holds `expected`, so a mismatch fails the pass); `copy_region` takes
`source_layer`, `source_frame`, `region`, `at` `[x,y]`; `map_colors` takes
`region` and `colors` `{"#from":"#to"}` (alpha must match); `flood_fill`
`seed`/`expected`/`color`; `brush` `points` plus `color`; `outline` `mode`
(outside|inside|recolor|erase). The full contracts and any command's flags
are one free call away: `describe edits | paint | outline | draw | animation
| motion | scenes | review`, `<command> -h`, `describe cli`.
Free for subscribers.

PixelLab AI-powered pixel art generation service.

Use of this service is subject to PixelLab's Terms of Service:
https://pixellab.ai/termsofservice

This MCP server provides programmatic access to generate:
- Characters with multiple directional views
- Character animations
- Isometric tiles
- Top-down tilesets for game maps
- Sidescroller tilesets for platformer games

All generation operations are non-blocking and return job IDs for status tracking.
Requires PixelLab subscription (with credit fallback support).

**Pixel tools (free, exact, you are the artist)**: one command line, pixelart_workbench(argv=[...]), inspects, edits, draws and animates pixel art by your own decisions; combine it with the AI tools above. Start with pixelart_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start'], mode='low'|'high') — low acts directly with few tokens, high plans out loud and reviews every frame. Animated effects (spells, hits, explosions, auras): vfx_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start']) — same ids, exports to the user's My effects.

**Git access**: Clone and push game project source code with standard git.
Use `list_projects` to see your projects and their git clone URLs.

exec tool declaration:
```ts
declare const tools: { mcp__pixellab__pixelart_workbench(args: {
  // One command line, e.g. 'lint <drawing_id> --rules outline_gap' or ['edit', '<id>', '--changes', '[…]']. Omit it for the playbook. A subject is an id or an image reference — never a file path; the server writes the output and returns a new id. A reference is `character:<id>:<direction>` for a rotation, `character:<id>:<direction>:<animation>` for every frame of that animation (the display name, type or [group: ...] id get_character prints), the same two forms for `object:<id>` (a one-direction object's direction is the literal `unknown`), `gallery:<id>`, `job:<id>`, `upload:<id>`, a data URL, an https link or base64. That is how a stored animation's pixels come back inline without downloading anything. Start with 'describe cli' for the full command list.
  argv?: string | Array<string> | null;
  // low (default): act directly, fewest tokens — one decisive image per result. high: think openly — fuller evidence and a review checklist; write your plan and observations in `notes`. Use the mode the user asked for.
  mode?: "low" | "high";
  // What you observed and what this step should achieve, in a few sentences (high mode: always; low: optional). On the first call, include the user's request. Stored with the step to improve these tools.
  notes?: string | null;
}): Promise<CallToolResult>; };
```"}

# Request and criteria handoff

Use for delegated asset work when a proposed production contract is ready to adopt, or when its consequential request/criteria change. The specialist prepares the contract; the calling agent independently compares its actual contents to the original assignment. This is an agent-to-agent review, not a new user-approval gate. Continue under established authorization when the contract is consistent.

## Specialist: return the exact proposed contract

Save a compact `request-review.json` in the consumer project. Point to existing artifacts instead of duplicating provider history or manufacturing PX2 state for a planning-only task. Its fields are:

- `version`: 1.
- `sources`: the brief and relevant consumer/reference sources, each with project-relative `path`, actual byte `sha256`, and `role`; include locators for the adopted decisions. Numbered locators refer to that individual file, never a concatenated multi-file terminal display. The caller verifies the cited content at those locators. Include the selected `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied one.
- `request`: `path`, `sha256`, `kind` (`provider_arguments` or `creative_brief`) and the actual tool name when known. Provider arguments must be the complete exact JSON to dispatch, including real reference inputs. Use a creative brief when an operation/schema has not been discovered; do not label it executable.
- `criteria`: `path` and `sha256` for the exact criteria to use. Each criterion has an ID, check, authority/basis, applicable scope and source locator. Distinguish owner/consumer requirements, specialist sample choices, observations and diagnostics.
- `choices`: the consequential specialist choices or unresolved decisions, where each appears in the request/criteria, and its reason. A criterion scoped to a chosen sample can assess that sample; it does not establish a universal project requirement.
- `resume`: existing store/task/output/job links when applicable. Omit absent production state.

Return the packet's path and SHA-256 to the caller. For PX2 production, link the saved request and Q records or an exact exported view with their state/record identity. Do not silently rebuild the request after review. Before dispatch, compare the actual arguments to the reviewed request; reference bytes/handles and non-text controls matter as much as prompt wording.

Keep a required outcome separate from the recipe proposed to achieve it. A qualitative requirement such as matching a reference or conveying a state still needs an acceptance criterion when its palette, geometry, frame count or layout are open. When demoting an unsupported recipe to a sample choice, preserve the underlying required outcome; do not leave only mechanical checks binding. Consumer code establishes its actual data/rendering behavior, not an unmeasured aesthetic quality. Attribute expert quality criteria to expert judgment where that is their basis.

Creative decisions within the assignment need not all go back to the user. For example, choosing a static first sample or a construction method is expert judgment; attributing it to an owner who specified only canvas dimensions is incorrect. Keep the choice explicit and scoped so it can be revised without changing the owner's brief. Observations alone do not become rejection rules.

### Measured facts in creative requests

Do not estimate pixel coordinates by eye and then describe them as verified. When a numerical image fact materially guides a request or verdict, retain the measurement with its source-image hash, frame and coordinate convention. The existing `asset-check --regions COLOR...` / `pixl_asset_check(regions=[...])` measures exact RGBA component boxes; it does not identify the subject or make those colors mandatory. Boxes use zero-based coordinates with exclusive right/bottom edges. For other measurements, save the reproducible calculation. When exact coordinates are unnecessary, describe the visual relationship and supply the actual reference instead.

Keep centering calculations in one coordinate convention. For a half-open box
`[left, top, right, bottom]`, its centre in pixel-edge coordinates is
`((left + right) / 2, (top + bottom) / 2)` and the canvas centre is `(width / 2, height / 2)`.
A centroid computed from zero-based pixel indices needs `+0.5` per axis to use those
same edge coordinates. A margin imbalance, box-centre offset and mass-centroid offset
are different quantities; retain the actual calculation before calling an asset centred.

The caller independently verifies consequential measured claims against the original image and measurement, including the coordinate convention; repeating a specialist's pixel map is not independent verification. Correct unsupported numbers before dispatch while preserving the required visual outcome.

## Resolve source evidence for the comparison

For candidate plans used by selected-asset preparation, call `pixl_request_review`
with the packet path and selected `asset_id` (CLI `request-review PACKET --asset ID
--root PROJECT`). It reads the exact request/criteria identities, returns cited text
with file-local bounds, and includes the current production continuation. It reports
invalid/unresolved locators and changed sources. A resolved excerpt is evidence for
the caller to interpret, not a consistency verdict. Retain this report with the review.

When the connection is already discovered, bind `request.provider` and
`request.connection: {path, sha256}` to its exact artifact. Preparation compares that
reviewed connection with the supplied one; host credentials stay outside the artifact.

Use `lines: [first,last]` on a criterion's source pointer when citing text; retain
`locator` as a human-readable label. Preparation validates explicit bounds before
saving new work. Numbered prose in older plans remains readable and receives
locator diagnostics. For non-text references inspect the actual image/animation;
for named sections resolve the location through the existing source tool. Do not
mark a locator verified merely because its claimed wording appears elsewhere.

The optional criterion `authority` uses PLAR's requirement/proposal/observation/unknown
labels. Keep its basis and scope explicit. This label is an assertion to compare,
not an automatic grant of owner authority.

## Caller: inspect before adopting

Open the packet and verify its hashes. Read the original brief, relevant sources, complete request and complete criteria, not just the specialist's summary or self-audit. Check:

1. Every explicit requirement survives into the request and relevant checks, including qualitative identity/style/state outcomes, actual reference role/input and consumer mapping. Check for dropped or weakened outcomes as well as added restrictions.
2. Every consequential extra restriction has its true basis and scope. Test whether a brief-conforming alternative would be rejected only because an observation or proposal was promoted to an owner requirement.
3. The proposed operation's actual declaration supports the payload. Do not infer a provider parameter, frame/direction count, alpha policy or camera from prose alone.
4. Findings concern these exact artifacts. Mechanical/hash validity and a specialist's consistency claim do not prove semantic agreement or artistic quality.
5. Each rejection rule belongs to the current candidate/stage and has satisfiable prerequisites. A first sample cannot require completed dependent family assets before it may be accepted. Retain deferred family or destination obligations with an explicit later stage in the handoff/PLAR; verify they remain scheduled rather than dropping the required outcome.

For each rejection criterion, save one concise comparison using the following
sequence. A table or JSON is sufficient; this is the caller's actual reasoning about
the source, not a worksheet to have the specialist certify for itself.

1. **Source obligation.** Derive the minimum required outcome from the original source
   wording and locator before using the draft criterion as its paraphrase. State what
   the source leaves open. For an expert criterion, identify the actual expert choice
   and candidate scope instead of inventing owner authority.
2. **Literal condition and additions.** Compare the entire check with that obligation.
   Identify the exact added or omitted words/clauses, including extent, composition,
   exclusions, comparisons and numerical bounds. A supported noun does not establish
   support for its modifiers. Read the check itself, not just its basis or label.
3. **Discriminating alternative.** For each added restriction, describe a plausible
   asset that keeps the source obligation true while making that specific restriction
   false. Name the clause being tested and whether the literal check would reject it.
   Merely changing a value the check already permits does not test that restriction.
   If the source itself excludes the alternative, identify the exact source support.
4. **Disposition.** Keep the required outcome; remove an unsupported narrowing from
   that rule or split it into an explicitly scoped expert choice with its own rationale.
   An ambiguous condition that could reject a valid alternative needs clearer wording;
   do not approve it by silently giving it a more permissive interpretation. Verify the
   correction in the returned artifact before marking the contract consistent.

For example, a requirement for a readable silhouette does not itself require an
outlined silhouette. Comparing two outline colours leaves the added outline rule
untested; a readable outline-free construction tests it. The specialist may still
recommend an outline for this sample and explain its artistic value. The comparison
preserves that expertise while accurately describing who chose it and what it binds.

Cover every rejection rule; group only genuinely identical ones. Retain the source
quote/bounds, literal delta, tested alternative and disposition together. A general
"the brief permits flexibility" statement or a prompt-choice label elsewhere cannot
cancel a restriction still present in an owner-authority acceptance condition.

Check the **review route** as well as the wording. A local mechanical check can
establish measured dimensions, frame counts or alpha values. It cannot decide which
shape is intentional foreground, whether a matte is unwanted, whether a silhouette
reads as the requested symbol, or whether an accent serves its role. For a mixed
criterion, either split the measurement and required visual judgment or set its mode
to `visual` (normally domain `visual` too). The runtime requires saved native/enlarged
candidate views for visual-mode or visual/continuity-domain reviews; labelling such a
condition `mechanical`/`local` bypasses that evidence requirement. A planning-only
# plar.txt format and operations

Version 1 is UTF-8 JSON, not a new programming language. The normative shape is [plar.schema.json](../../../runtime/pixl/plar.schema.json). A complete worked project is [the queue UI example](../../../resources/examples/plar-project/README.md). Read its source before its example requirements.

Top-level fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| version | `1` |
| project | `name` and concise `brief`; no absolute installation paths |
| coverage | Arrays `included`, `excluded`, `unresolved`; explicit scan boundary and blind spots |
| sources | Stable `id`, project-relative `path`, optional `sha256`; saves bind existing files without a hash |
| assets | Stable rows described below; an empty list is valid when the inspected scope requires no production art |

Each asset has `id`, `kind`, `purpose`, `status`, `consumers`, `existing`, `requirements`, `delivery`, `depends_on`, `questions`, `next`, and `evidence`. Optional `production` links `store`, `task`, `output`. Optional `references` names visual inputs as described below. Kind is a descriptive string; UI panels, fonts, atlases and normal maps need not pretend to be sprites here. Translate to the actual PIXL/provider contract during production.

- `consumers`: `{source, symbol, usage}`; source is an ID from the sources table. Symbol and usage explain the binding, not merely a filename.
- `references`: `{source, role, instructions}`; source is a bound source ID. Role is `style`, `identity`, `pose`, `layout`, `palette`, `mask` or `motion`. Instructions say what to preserve. These are optional for text-only briefs; a filename mentioned in a requirement is not provider image transport.
- `existing`: `{path, role}`; role explains reusable/placeholder/reference or other current use. Missing paths are reported, not rejected.
- `requirements`: `{property, value, authority, sources, reason}`. Value is JSON; authority is `requirement`, `observation`, `proposal`, or `unknown`. Sources is an array of source IDs. An empty array is useful for an explicit unsourced proposal/unknown; support adopted requirements with addressable evidence.
- `delivery`: `{path, checks}`; exact destination (file or package path) and applicable mechanical, visual and consumer/import checks.
- `depends_on`: other asset IDs; cycles and dangling IDs are rejected.
- `questions`: unresolved choices relevant to this asset. `next`: one actionable instruction.
- `evidence`: `{path, note}` links to retained results. Source-bind evidence that must remain byte-identical.
- `status`: `todo`, `in_progress`, `review`, `integrated`, or `deferred`. Status is authored by the host. File existence does not prove integration or quality.

All paths are relative to the consumer root and use forward slashes. Source hashes detect local drift; they do not prove the interpretation of the source. The reader reports changed/missing/unbound sources and missing files. It does not restamp changed sources, guess readiness, contact PixelLab or certify artistic quality. Refresh a hash only after re-reading and reconciling the dependent claims. Focused reads include the full transitive dependency rows and their issues, so a caller does not lose the style baseline or an unresolved source when delegating a dependent asset.

## MCP

`pixl_plar_read({})` returns the queue, project scope and source binding results. To select an asset:

```json
{"asset_id":"queue.working"}
```

Save through `pixl_plar_save` with `document` holding the complete JSON document and `expect` equal to the last returned file hash, or `"new"` for creation. Optional `path` defaults to `plar.txt`. A stale write is rejected; re-read and merge. Previous changed bytes are retained under `.pixl/plar-history/`. Keep independent queues in separate files when project scope requires it.

Use `pixl_commit({store,expect,document})` for a PX2 document with its next revision. The JSON record format uses `{"$ref":"id"}` and `{"$symbol":"value"}`. Exactly one of `document` or the existing `candidate` wire-file path is accepted. The same revision, dependency, evidence and acceptance checks apply. PLAR does not automatically invent PX2 decisions or criteria.

## CLI and portability

Resolve the plugin runner relative to this skill, then use its **absolute** path with the target project root:

```text
python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py plar read --root /ABS/PROJECT
python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py plar read --root /ABS/PROJECT --asset queue.working
python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py plar save /ABS/document.json --root /ABS/PROJECT --expect new
python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py commit /ABS/PROJECT/.pixl /ABS/plan.json --json --expect STATE_HASH --root /ABS/PROJECT
```

Copy/install the complete plugin, not the skill directory alone. Requirements and outputs stay in the consumer project. The CLI can support a host without MCP; the MCP server exposes the same deterministic operations when configured with that root.

## Focused delegation identity

A selected read returns `project_root`, `requirements_hash`, `asset`, full `dependencies`, relevant `sources`, `visual_references` and a derived `production` view. Source rows add `observed_sha256` and `absolute_path`; stored source paths remain portable and relative. The full queue's existing `hash` is still the compare-and-swap token for saves.

The requirements hash covers the selected asset and transitive dependency requirements, their bound/current source identities and project brief. It excludes status, next action, evidence lists, production-state links and absolute installation paths. It does not assert readiness or acceptance; read dependency status/issues separately. Changing a style reference changes this hash even before someone refreshes its saved source hash. An unrelated asset's queue progress does not.

This additive version-1 extension keeps existing documents valid. Use a runtime containing the reference-role extension to author documents with `references`; older closed-schema readers cannot interpret new fields.

## Selective refresh

Queue reads include `changes`: tracked source drift, direct and transitively affected asset IDs, and unaffected IDs. Pass `since` (CLI `--since`) with a retained prior PLAR byte hash to compare declarations as well. Saves return this comparison against the replaced version. Queue progress fields (`status`, `next`, `evidence`, `production`) are not requirement changes. Coverage changes are reported separately. History bytes are hash-checked before comparison. Use `since` on the whole queue, then select an affected asset; focused reads include `dependency_issues`.

This is conservative file/dependency impact, not a semantic code scanner. Re-read changed code and look for new states, consumers or dynamic paths. A shared source edit can affect several rows for review without requiring all their requirements or assets to change. Do not merely refresh hashes. Keep stable roles/IDs on destination moves; retain superseded work as deferred where applicable.

[First-candidate preparation](prepare.md) consumes a focused selection and the exact reviewed request/criteria artifacts, removing handwritten PX2 setup from that path.

## Allocation and production continuity

A focused read joins the selected row to its retained PX2 store. `production` reports
current task/output acceptance, selection identity, provider-bound pending jobs and
one next action. Missing or invalid state is an explicit diagnostic while the
requirements remain readable. Queue `status` remains an authored progress label.
`new_request_allowed` is only a local selection/pending-work advisory; preparation
still validates the exact reviewed request, current source identity and connection.

After the selected task is accepted, `production.delivery` compares its nominated
bytes with the declared destination and reports every saved containing family's
current acceptance and manifest. `next_action: delivered` requires matching bytes,
current requirements and completed containing families, including current explicit
PLAR selections for their production members; it creates no new verdict. An older
sample baseline retains its historical contract and separately scoped adoption.
Missing/changed destination files or unfinished collective review keep
`review_delivery`. Pending jobs and changed requirements retain their earlier
recovery priority. The authored `integrated` label cannot establish completion.

Single-output preparation links the resulting store/task/output and snapshot evidence
back to the row. A failed concurrent queue save leaves the prepared job intact; resume
the same preparation to repair its link. The default asset store is discoverable;
custom stores require the existing link or explicit store argument. Multiple outputs
need a deliberate choice of the delivery output.

Source changes require review of affected/dependent rows, not automatic replacement
of all art. For a revised contract, reconcile pending work on its original connection,
retain the reviewed new packet, then use `plar prepare --revise --expect STATE_HASH`.
The new generation is appended to the existing store; prior inputs, jobs, candidates
and verdicts remain. Use returned IDs. Historical acceptance describes its original
contract and cannot complete the newly selected generation.

# Exact request and criterion review evidence

`request-review PACKET --root ROOT [--asset ID] [--plar PATH]` and
`pixl_request_review({packet, asset_id?, path?})` expose the same read-only report.
They resolve the existing version-1 request-review packet and candidate-plan JSON.
They do not write a caller review, classify semantic consistency, or authorize a
provider call. The [skill procedure](../plugins/pixl/skills/pixl/references/request-review.md)
assigns the actual comparison to the calling agent.

The report verifies request/criteria byte hashes and returns their exact arguments,
criterion checks, stated bases/authority/scopes, candidate controls and packet choices.
All packet source identities are checked, including references not cited by criteria.
An optional request.connection path/hash binds the exact connection artifact, and
request.provider binds its provider name. Reports verify the artifact identity; new
preparation requires the supplied connection to equal the reviewed one. Existing
packets without these optional assertions keep their previous preparation contract.
Criterion source references produce file-local excerpts or explicit diagnostics for
changed, unavailable, binary, invalid, unresolved or excessively broad locations.
`consistent` remains null and `caller_comparison` remains unperformed. A valid source
range does not show that the requirement entails the authored rejection condition.

Candidate criteria may add `authority` (requirement, proposal, observation, unknown).
A text source pointer may add `lines: [first,last]`, with one-based inclusive integer
bounds, alongside its existing path/locator. Explicit bounds are validated before new
preparation. These optional additions preserve earlier plans and immutable history;
older closed-schema writers do not support authoring the additional fields.

Legacy prose using `line N` or `lines N-M` receives range diagnostics. Other locator
forms remain explicitly unresolved; they are not silently interpreted as verified.
Binary references require actual host inspection. Each source excerpt is bounded;
overlarge ranges return a request to narrow them rather than truncated evidence.
Report reads and preparation honor the same confined consumer paths.

Supplying an asset ID also compares the packet's selected requirements identity and
includes current production. The focused production `continuation` contains the exact
state hash, current task, provider/remote job identities with original discovery,
immediate action, prerequisites before another request, and outcome-dependent next
steps. Pending jobs require their original connection's observation/reconciliation.
Succeeded results lead to retrieval/import or candidate review before a correction
is proposed; actual unavailability can be recorded. A done task leads to delivery
review. Missing or stale selection remains explicit.

These are derived workflow instructions, not additional automatic approval rules.
The existing `new_request_allowed` field remains the local selection/pending advisory;
it does not mean the result was reviewed or another request is needed. Carry the
continuation into the caller result and reread after observations/state changes.
The report neither transfers a simulated job to a live service nor treats source-path
integration as renderer or artistic acceptance.

## Exact PLAR handoff snapshot

`pixl_plar_handoff` / `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --asset ID --requirements HASH
--expect STATE_HASH --root ROOT [--path plar.txt]` retains a consumer-owned JSON file
under `.pixl/handoffs/`, named by its byte hash. It verifies expected selected
requirements and production state, preserves the entire derived `resume` and its
immediate `next`, and stores agent-authored judgments under `details`. It returns the
snapshot path/hash and relevant identities. Identical input/state is idempotent;
changed details or state produce another snapshot. Corrupt existing bytes are rejected.

Details require an assignment `status` (delivered/partial/needs_input/blocked), with
other relevant artifacts/checks/reasoning fields chosen by the agent. Reserved derived
field names cannot be inserted at the top of details. Completed caller actions and
future work belong under their own details fields; they do not rewrite `resume` or
`next`. This is no automatic artistic verdict or completion certificate. State and
PLAR remain unchanged. The snapshot describes the observed point in time; reread the
selected asset before acting, especially after another agent changes it. A missing
production continuation leaves the ordinary allocation diagnostic usable without
manufacturing a stateful handoff. Existing handoff files remain supported as history.

project.name: Queue status UI
project.brief: Allocate coherent pixel-art Working, Ready, Retry and Paused status assets for shared 16x16 queue cells while preserving the existing Start vector. Review a representative sample before family expansion; this allocation performs no asset generation.

included: Read BRIEF.md and SOURCE-MAP.md in full; re-read the changed brief, queue-state and queue-view source for this refresh.
Resolve the local ./queue type import and trace started/ok/error/pause through stateAfter to running/succeeded/failed/paused visual descriptors.
Trace both statusCell and compactStatus to the same statusVisuals map; allocate one shared asset per status rather than duplicate assets per consumer.
Inspect the only checked-in art, assets/start.svg, at source level for shape, dimensions and accent; verify the four current PNG destinations are absent.
Reconcile the Retry destination move to assets/error-retry.png while preserving its queue.retry ID and unchanged failure/retry purpose.
Capture unchanged display.cell, scale, nearest filtering, frameMs and dark-panel color from the supplied view descriptor.

Current refresh: re-read BRIEF.md line 9 and src/queue-view.ts; retain queue.ready ID while moving its destination to assets/ready-confirmed.png and promoting the explicitly required asymmetrical-arm check mark. Other states and Start unchanged.

RENDER-STAGE continuation: actual supplied browser entry imports src/queue.ts and queue-view.ts; caller captured transitions and both consumers, specialist and caller opened native/enlarged panel views and destination. Ready scoped style adopted; all earlier coverage statements above retain their historical allocation/refresh scopes.

RENDER-RECHECK guided repair: unchanged separately versioned helper captured both actual consumers in one CDP page; viewport 1280x1000, all eight available Start/Ready bounds matched screenshot; native/enlarged views inspected. Earlier failure retained.

PRODUCTION-STAGE: real official PixelLab generated Working seed, Retry and Paused; failed transparent Paused and failed AIanimation retained; official guarded background edits and seed-based motion construction; all members and exact package rendered in both actual consumers at1x/3x including live100ms playback; scoped color/grayscale collective review passed.

AUTHORING update: inspected shared statusCell/compactStatus descriptors and renderer paint/animate; no reduced-motion mapping currently exists. Retained prepared request and historical plan; no consumer/source edit or remote generation.
excluded: Server-registry account badges returned by accountBadge are explicitly outside this local request; do not allocate replacement badge art.
No images are allocated for stateAfter or other functions without a visual role; the queue transitions determine status meaning only.

Historical render-stage scope, superseded for generation by PRODUCTION-STAGE.md: No new Start control, panel background, font, text label, host configuration, generated art or provider operation is assigned.
unresolved: Account badge server registry remains outside this local asset request.
Broader generated quality and unaided nativeClaude/Codex production remain unproven by this maintainer-operated continuation.
Historical Ready requirement/selection drift remains explicit; old request and verdict identities are unchanged.
Authoring branch stationary reduced-motion Working mapping and contract need independent caller review; old prepared animation request blocked.

queue.purpose: Show successful completion as Ready in both full and compact status cells; propose this as the representative family sample.
queue.next: Available-member destination verification now passes through both actual consumers; scoped style unchanged. Preserve historical selection drift and review_contract diagnostic; do not rebind old jobs or transfer old verdicts. Next useful family production action is reviewed Working four-frame activity strip against adopted Ready baseline under future authorization.

queue.purpose: Communicate ongoing work in both full and compact status cells without implying success. Caller update for this authoring branch: the reduced-motion mode must use a stationary Working symbol distinguishable from Ready and Paused. Confirm its consumer mapping before any further generation.
queue.next: Resolve retained prepared Working intent through caller comparison; define branch-only stationary reduced-motion mapping and contract for both consumers before separately assigned revised preparation. Do not dispatch the old animation-only request.

queue.purpose: Show failed work and the Retry action in both full and compact status cells with a shape that remains distinguishable without color.
queue.next: Read production prerequisites; prepare the selected stage when its inputs are accepted.

queue.purpose: Retain the existing idle Start control shared by both status consumers.
queue.next: Preserve the existing vector file and idle mapping during future status integration; no new Start asset is allocated.

queue.purpose: Show paused work in both full and compact status cells, distinguishable from activity, completion and retry without color alone.
queue.next: Read production prerequisites; prepare the selected stage when its inputs are accepted.

changes.scope: Tracked source bindings and declarations only; inspect source/coverage for newly introduced or dynamic consumers.
